Data centers create a heat island effect, warming the nearby areas by an average of 3.6° with the highest measurement reaching an increase of 16.4°.

Not only have communities seen typical examples of environmental injustice, but some have experienced an exponential rise in traffic accidents coinciding with data center development. In rural Louisiana "[o]n the roads surrounding Meta's construction site, vehicle crashes have gone up by more than 600%."

Individuals living nearby data centers have reported their water tasting or looking different since the development of data centers in their area, and continue to be concerned about the quality of their water necessary for daily living. Mass water usage can lead to shortages, especially if a given area is at risk of drought conditions. As climate change worsens making drought more frequent and water scarcity a severe issue, we simply cannot afford to use mass amounts of water on data centers.
